subject: Business Models
title: The Survivorship Bias Problem
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Survivorship Bias Problem.

hook.text: We study Amazon, Apple, and Google obsessively. We ignore 10,000 companies that tried the same things and failed.

buildup.text: Survivorship bias: we learn from winners and assume their strategies cause success. We don't study the dead.

discovery.text: Many failed companies did exactly what successful ones did: pivoted fast, raised capital, hired great teams.

twist.text: For every Facebook, there were 100 social networks. For every Uber, 50 ride-sharing apps. Success includes luck.

climax.text: Studying failures teaches more than studying successes. The dead reveal which strategies actually don't work.

punchline.text: For every success, 100 failures tried the same. Study the dead, not the living.

quiz.question: What is survivorship bias in business?
options: Focusing only on surviving companies and ignoring failures that used similar strategies
Companies that survive are always better
